source.title: SAEmnesia: Erasing Concepts in Diffusion Models with Supervised Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: E. Cassano; Riccardo Renzulli; Marco Nurisso; Mirko Zaffaroni; A. Perotti; Marco Grangetto

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. The text gives an arXiv version date in 2026 and an ICML 2026 venue despite the supplied year of 2025; this does not prevent reading the study.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features as units for targeted concept erasure and deliberately trains supervised mappings. Its results concern induced feature centralization in diffusion-model SAEs, not whether models naturally have the neuron-pole job distribution asserted in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: SAEmnesia's supervised losses explicitly promote concept-to-latent assignments, so its centralization results are not an audit of naturally occurring neuron jobs. The paper also compares unlearning performance, but those outcomes do not test the listed claim versions. The k-NN plot compares the top-scoring latent, all features, random features, and random guess; the text explicitly reports only that the top-scoring latent is nearly as accurate as all features through most timesteps.
record.test_reason: The study trains supervised SAEs on SD v1.5 diffusion activations to force one-to-one concept–latent mappings for concept erasure. It induces centralization on purpose and reports unlearning performance. It does not audit a model's own neurons, InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons, attribution graphs, or held-out explanation scoring, so its results bear on no claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that supervised SAE training prevents feature splitting and yields concept-aligned latents. This gives more efficient and effective concept erasure in diffusion models than unsupervised SAEs. They make no claim about natural neuron interpretability in language models.
record.recipe_differences: This is a supervised SAE framework for concept erasure in diffusion models, not an audit of language-model neuron poles or held-out natural-language neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature-centralization examples vary by concept. The paper also reports that SAEmnesia variants and training configurations differ in unlearning performance and multiplier sensitivity, but these are not tests of the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Supervised SAE training on SD v1.5 cross-attention activations gives higher, single-peak feature-concept scores than unsupervised SAeUron: Flowers 0.0404 vs 0.0166; Architectures, Rabbits and Sea similar. A single top latent nearly matches all-feature k-NN accuracy across most timesteps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised losses can concentrate concept information into single SAE latents in diffusion models, whereas unsupervised SAEs spread concepts across many latents (feature splitting).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Centralization is deliberately induced by supervised losses and uses SAE latents, so it does not establish that the base model's own neurons naturally have one main job. The principal evaluation is on SD v1.5 and selected concepts; the authors note within-group interference and limitations in scaling to very large concept vocabularies. Some illustrated score values are available only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning accuracy, retention, FID, adversarial robustness, sequential unlearning, and nudity-removal outcomes were left out because they measure concept-erasure performance rather than neuron or latent interpretability. The k-NN plot's random-feature and random-guess results were not extracted as separate rows because their outcomes are not described numerically in the text.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job shares.
No language models, MoE models or scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 or analysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No estimate of the interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture or tools. Supervised SAE latents are imposed, not the model's own neurons.
No attribution graphs or circuit analysis.
No test of explanations against held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's framing that unsupervised SAEs show feature splitting concerns SAE latents, not base-model neurons, so it does not bear on V4. The text gives an ICML 2026 venue and a v3 date in 2026.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole proportions, or independent explanation testing.
No audit of language models, dense or mixture-of-experts scaling, or trillion-parameter models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.

No InceptionV1-sized vision-model interpretability-share estimate or comparison of architecture/tool effects on that share. The study imposes supervised concept assignments in diffusion-model SAEs rather than testing natural neuron interpretability.
No attribution graphs or test of whether a model's own neurons suffice to explain behavior.
No test of explanations against activations beyond the examples used to write them.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by predicting activations on new text.
